newsitem.title: USA: NBC, National Geographic to launch cable channel.
newsitem.headline: NBC, National Geographic to launch cable channel.

text.p: General Electric Co's National Broadcasting Co unit and the National Geographic Society said they will launch a new National Geographic cable television channel in 1997.
The companies said the new channel will be a 50-50 joint venture. The channel will be launched in the United States as well globally. The new channel was announced during a telephone news conference.
Executives declined to detail the cost of the startup. Society and NBC said its business plan was not yet completed.

"The guts of the relationship will be finding partners in making equity investments in the underlying channel," said Stuart Goldfarb, an NBC senior vice president. "It's going to be heavily premised on local partners getting involved as equity partners in local (country) channels."
Goldfarb said the channel was not likely to be launched in the U.S. in 1997 because there was no current channel capacity among U.S. cable operators.
"We would be looking at targeting international markets," Goldfarb said. "We are currently in discussions with a number of potential partners."
The first launch sites will most likely be Latin America, Europe and Asia, officials said.
Tim Kelly, president of National Geographic Television, said there were "several hundred hours" of programming available for the new channel.
Kelly said the channel would include children's and dramatic programming as well as documentaries.
"We expect to produce or acquire a variety of programming for the channel," said Kelly. "A lot of producers are coming to us as filmmakers and broadcast partners."
National Geographic said it expected to continue its broadcasting deals with Turner Broadcasting System Inc and the Public Broadcasting Service in the U.S.
The channels would operate for 24 hours, be advertiser supported and broadcast in the local language.
National Geographic said it would acquire other programming for the channel.
